questions.prompt: In offline RL, why is a maximum over all actions in the Bellman target risky?
options: It only works for continuous action spaces, so discrete tasks cannot use a maximum at all
It makes the target independent of the next state, so learning from the data stalls entirely
It forces the learned policy to be deterministic, which removes all of its remaining stochasticity
It selects actions whose value estimates are extrapolations that the dataset can never correct
questions.explanation: The maximum seeks the largest estimate, which tends to be at unsupported actions where estimates are unconstrained by data and cannot be corrected by new experience.
questions.skillLabel: Know why max over unsupported actions is risky

questions.prompt: A line fitted to rewards 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 at actions 0, 1, 2 is used to estimate the reward at action 5. Estimate? (one decimal)
Estimated rewards (0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6); support {0, 1, 2}. Penalty weight lambda needed so that action 2 beats unsupported action 4 under Q - lambda*distance? (two decimals)
Mean reward 1.2 from n = 4 samples, sigma = 1, c = 1. What is the lower confidence bound mean - c*sigma/sqrt(n)? (two decimals)
Which statement about conservative offline RL is correct?
options: It requires much more online interaction with the real environment to stay safe
It removes the need for any value function or critic in the learning procedure
It always matches the optimal policy of the task, even for actions outside the data
It trades some regret inside the data for protection from errors outside it
questions.explanation: Conservatism cannot find value that lies outside the data; it avoids relying on unreliable estimates there.

questions.prompt: Explain how an overestimate at an unsupported action at step 2 can spoil the value of a supported action at step 1.
rubric: The target of step 1 uses a max over step-2 actions
The max picks the overestimated unsupported action
The inflated target is assigned to the supported step-1 action and repeated backups accumulate it
